title: Potato Production Technology, Seed Plot Technique & Late Blight Protocol
source: ICAR - Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI), Shimla
content: Potato (Solanum tuberosum) is a cool-season tuber crop. Soil: Loose, friable sandy loam rich in organic matter, pH 5.5 to 6.5. Seed preparation: Use certified disease-free seed tubers of 30-40 g size (diameter 35-45 mm) having 2-3 well-sprouted chits (eyes). Treat tubers with Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/litre for 10 minutes to prevent black scurf and dry rot. Planting: 60 cm ridge-to-ridge and 20 cm tuber-to-tuber. Earthing-up: Perform first earthing-up at 25-30 DAS when plants reach 15-20 cm height, and second earthing-up at 45 DAS to prevent greening of developing tubers caused by sunlight exposure. Fertilizer: 150-180 kg N, 80-100 kg P2O5, and 100-120 kg K2O per hectare. Potassium improves tuber size and starch content; use MOP (Muriate of Potash) or SOP. Late blight emergency alert: During cloudy, foggy weather with high humidity (>90%) and temp 10-20°C, spray Mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/l before onset; if blight symptoms appear, immediately spray Dimethomorph 50 WP @ 1 g/litre or Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/l.
